the NMDA receptor is involved in the regulation of GABAA receptors in granule neurons in the developing cerebellum, and that this regulation is mediated by the γ subunit.

NMDA receptor antagonists, such as MK‐801, may alter GABAA receptor subunit expression during development and that the changes in receptor pharmacology that result from such treatments may have long‐term consequences for the development of the cerebellum and other regions of the brain.

The main takeaway from our work is that
NMDA receptor activation is necessary for the maturation of GABAA receptors, and this process is sensitive to the developmental stage of the neuron.
the GABAA receptor is not a static entity but rather is subject to modulation throughout development, and this modulation is influenced by the environment in which the cells are growing.
